gen-dafont-joystix-gf-cascadia-code: Chunky arcade lettering up top, almost stamped in brass. Joystix spaces itself wide and stays compact in height, and Cascadia Code supplies a wire-thin monoline path that glides smoothly around every bend.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono reads like pins standing in a wide board, every curve as thick as its stems. And Joystix, with its slightly stressed curves, is the one that brings arcade swagger, so the contrast in character is the real hook.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-julius-sans-one: Arcade punch meets quiet spacing. Joystix has thin strokes about half the weight of its thick ones, while Julius Sans One sets its stems and arches at identical thickness with wide gaps between letters.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-lexend-exa: Lexend Exa reads wide and stout, with curves that stay open and stubby ascenders over a big x-height. Joystix is only mildly stressed between stem and connecting stroke, so give Lexend Exa a little extra size to let those broad forms breathe.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-lexend-giga: Lexend Giga draws flat, single-weight lines like a fineliner, with generous tracking that opens up each word. But Joystix has a modest thick-thin difference and a bold arcade attitude, so a slightly larger Lexend Giga keeps the two in step.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-lexend-mega: Approachable is the first word for Lexend Mega, drawn as if with one nib and with a body height close to the capitals. Its r, n and m have arches matching their stems, while Joystix carries a faint pressure shadow like worn charcoal.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-lexend-peta: Arcade bluntness, then a wide-mouthed body. Joystix is best at bold, tracked-out display lettering, and Lexend Peta is best at big, contrast-free curves that run from stem to terminal without thinning.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-lexend-tera: Lexend Tera reads like a plotter pen at work, one single-weight line with open curves and letters spaced like stepping stones. So a long passage moves steadily, while Joystix keeps its thicks mild and its arcade mood bold.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-montserrat-alterna: Montserrat Alternates has a c as open as a bent paperclip, with round letters whose rims match the stems. And Joystix, with slight but visible thick-thin variation, can sit at a larger size while the body stays modest.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-cascadia-mono: Friendly is the first impression of Junegull, whose closed, pinched letterforms look cast in iron. And Cascadia Mono opens up beneath it as a plain sans, so the two feel like a vintage sign beside a tidy ledger.
